f: Step 1: |H| at 3-dB = 687 / sqrt(2). Step 2: = 485.782. Check: (485.782)^2 is approximately half of 687^2 = 471969, confirming half power.

q: A signal band-limited to fm = 1091 kHz has Nyquist rate:
h: Nyquist rate = 2 fm.
f: Step 1: rate = 2 x 1091 kHz. Step 2: = 2182 kHz minimum sampling rate. Check: sampling exactly at this rate is phase-sensitive, so real systems add margin and an anti-alias filter.

q: A noiseless B = 1229 kHz channel must carry 7374 kbps by the Nyquist formula. The number of signal levels L needed is:
h: Rate = 2B log2(L); solve for L.
f: Step 1: log2(L) = 7374 / (2 x 1229) = 3. Step 2: L = 2^3 = 8. Check: L is a power of two, as a whole number of bits per symbol requires.

q: An AM carrier has Pc = 451 W and modulation index mu = 0.27. Total transmitted power is:
h: Ptot = Pc (1 + mu^2 / 2).
f: Step 1: mu^2/2 = 0.0365. Step 2: Ptot = 451 x 1.0365 = 467.44 W. Check: sideband efficiency rises with mu and peaks at 33 percent when mu = 1, motivating DSB-SC and SSB.

q: A continuous-time state model has dominant eigenvalue lambda = -983 (real). The free response is: (spaced-repetition variant 9442)
o: Decided by the C matrix alone
Stable: dominant eigenvalue has negative real part (CT)
Stable because the eigenvalue is real
Stable for every input matrix B
h: CT state stability follows eigenvalue real parts, as with s-plane poles.
f: Step 1: the mode behaves as e^(-983 t). Step 2: it decays, so the model is stable. Check: this is the same left-half-plane rule as Module 5, stated for A.

q: A discrete-time sinusoid cos(pi 835/643 n) has fundamental period N0 =
h: Need Omega0 N / (2 pi) to be an integer, with Omega0 = pi m/k in lowest terms.
f: Step 1: Omega0/(2 pi) = 835/1286 after reduction. Step 2: smallest N making Omega0 N a multiple of 2 pi is N = 1286. Check: Omega0 x 1286 / pi = 1670, an even integer multiple relationship holds: True.

q: For x[n] = (-0.6819)^n u[n], the value x[2] is:
h: Raise alpha to the power n; u[n] = 1 for n at least 0.
f: Step 1: x[2] = (-0.6819)^2. Step 2: value = 0.465. Check: |alpha| = 0.6819 is below 1, so the sequence decays.

q: A memoryless system is y = x^2 (sample values). Feeding the single sample x = 82 + 232 gives output:
h: Apply the rule to the summed input, do not sum separate outputs.
f: Step 1: summed input = 314. Step 2: y = (314)^2 = 98596. Check: separate outputs would sum to 60548, which differs, proving nonlinearity.

q: For x(t) = u(t) and h(t) = u(t) in a continuous-time LTI system, y(102) is: (spaced-repetition variant 9443)
h: The output is the ramp r(t) = t u(t).
f: Step 1: y(t) = integral from 0 to t of 1 dt = t for t at least 0. Step 2: y(102) = 102. Check: differentiating y returns u(t), the step response relationship h = ds/dt holds.

q: X(s) = 322 / (s (s + 264)). The final value x(infinity) is:
h: Final-value theorem: limit of s X(s) as s tends to 0.
f: Step 1: s X(s) = 322/(s + 264). Step 2: at s = 0 this is 322/264 = 1.2197. Check: the remaining pole at -264 is in the left-half plane, so the theorem applies.

q: y[n] - 0.5386 y[n - 1] = x[n]. The pole of H(z) is at z =
h: Transform: Y(z) (1 - a z^-1) = X(z); the pole solves 1 - a z^-1 = 0.
f: Step 1: H(z) = 1 / (1 - 0.5386 z^-1). Step 2: denominator zero when z = 0.5386. Check: this matches the pair a^n u[n] with a = 0.5386.

q: A sawtooth-type Fourier series has harmonic coefficients b_k = 2A/(k pi). For A = 336 and k = 55, b_k is:
h: Substitute A and k into 2A/(k pi).
f: Step 1: b_k = 2 x 336 / (55 pi). Step 2: = 3.8892 (4 decimal places). Check: coefficients fall as 1/k, slower than a triangle wave (1/k^2) but faster than the constant spectrum of an impulse train.

q: A DFT uses N = 16384 samples taken at fs = 1753088 Hz. The bin spacing is: (spaced-repetition variant 9443)
h: Spacing = fs / N.
f: Step 1: spacing = 1753088 / 16384. Step 2: = 107 Hz between bins X[k] and X[k+1]. Check: N bins x 107 Hz spans the full 1753088 Hz sampling rate.

q: Output power is 15.02 times the input power. The gain in decibels is:
h: dB = 10 log10(P2/P1) for powers (20 log10 is for voltages).
f: Step 1: ratio = 15.02. Step 2: 10 log10(15.02) = 11.77 dB. Check: ratio 0.5 gives about -3 dB and ratio 10 gives +10 dB; sign follows gain versus loss.

q: A 16-ary modulation runs at 938 baud. Its bit rate is:
h: Bit rate = baud x log2(L).
f: Step 1: bits per symbol = log2(16) = 4. Step 2: bit rate = 938 x 4 = 3752 bps. Check: denser constellations raise rate at fixed baud but need higher SNR for the same error rate.

q: For A = [[0, 1], [-833, -175]] (companion form), det(A) is:
h: det [[p, q],[r, s]] = p s - q r.
f: Step 1: det = (0)(-175) - (1)(-833). Step 2: = 833. Check: det(A) equals the product of eigenvalues, here the constant term of s^2 + 175 s + 833.

q: For x(t) = 118 cos(2 pi 288 t) (1 ohm reference), the average power P is:
h: P = A^2 / 2 for any sinusoid, independent of frequency.
f: Step 1: identify amplitude A = 118. Step 2: P = A^2/2 = 13924/2 = 6962. Check: average of cos^2 over a period is 1/2, and frequency 288 Hz does not change the average.

q: Evaluate the integral over all t of (t^2 + 382) delta(t - (59)) dt:
h: Sifting: the impulse samples the bracket at t = t0.
f: Step 1: sifting property: integral of x(t) delta(t - t0) dt = x(t0). Step 2: x(59) = 59^2 + 382 = 3863. Check: everything away from t = 59 is multiplied by zero.

q: The system y[n] = x[n] + x[n - 645] is classified as: (spaced-repetition variant 9444)
o: With memory, causal, linear and time-invariant
With memory and noncausal
Memoryless and causal
Memoryless and noncausal
h: It uses the present sample and a past sample only.
f: Step 1: x[n - 645] is a past sample, so the system has memory. Step 2: no future samples appear, so it is causal. Step 3: it is a fixed linear combination with constant coefficients, hence linear and time-invariant.

q: Convolving x[n] = {865, 154} with h[n] = {204, 700} (both starting at n = 0), the value y[1] is:
X(s) = 1 / ((s + 5)(s + 444)) with causal ROC. In x(t), the coefficient multiplying e^(-5 t) is:
h: Cover-up: set s = -a in 1/(s + b).
f: Step 1: partial fractions: A/(s+5) + B/(s+444) with A = 1/(444 - 5) = 0.0023. Step 2: x(t) = (0.0023 e^(-5 t) - 0.0023 e^(-444 t)) u(t). Check: x(0+) = 0, matching the initial-value behaviour of this strictly proper X(s).
